name: Michael Banf
tagline: Machine learning for gene regulation, graphs and the factory floor.
intro: I am a machine-learning researcher and engineer at Perelyn in Munich. My work sits where probabilistic modelling meets messy real systems: gene regulatory networks and transcription-factor binding in plants, geometric and topological deep learning, knowledge graphs for language-model agents, and condition monitoring in manufacturing. I did a PhD in computer vision at the University of Siegen, a postdoc in computational biology at the Carnegie Institution for Science at Stanford, and spent several years building industrial ML at fabforce before joining Perelyn.
